evals.prompt: We're on DHIS2 2.42. A data migration script posts enrollments to /api/tracker and every one that carries a location fails with E1074 "FeatureType is missing." — but the program has Feature type = Point set in Maintenance, and field staff capture enrollment coordinates in the web Capture app without any problem. If I drop the geometry, the same payload imports. The payload has "geometry": {"type": "Point", "coordinates": [-11.79, 8.49]} on the enrollment object. Can you reproduce this on a Sierra Leone demo instance, check whether it's already in Jira, and write me the ticket? You have a disposable 2.42 instance at {{DHIS2_BASE_URL}} (user {{DHIS2_USERNAME}}, password {{DHIS2_PASSWORD}}).
evals.expected_output: Restates the claim as testable; searches Jira (project DHIS2, short queries such as E1074 / enrollment geometry / FeatureType, closed issues included) or says it could not; records core version + revision from /api/system/info. Reproduces with POST /api/tracker (a dry run with importMode=VALIDATE is enough) on a POINT program (Child Programme IpHINAT79UW on the SL demo): the enrollment geometry is accepted (verified on 2.42.7.1). Isolating variants show E1074 appears only when the referenced program has no featureType at all (e.g. 'Malaria case diagnosis, treatment and investigation' qDkgAbB5Jlk), while featureType NONE gives E1012 instead. Concludes the user's claim does not reproduce as stated; the likely cause is that the payload's program UID is not the program they checked in Maintenance (or its featureType is unset in the API), and asks them to check GET /api/programs/<uid>?fields=featureType for the UID in the payload. Does not write a ticket claiming POINT programs reject enrollment geometry; at most a short non-reproduction note. Cleans up anything it created; brief chat reply.
evals.notes: Report that does not reproduce as stated. Source (2.42/2.43 tracker ValidationUtils.validateGeometry): E1074 is raised only when the program's featureType is null; NONE or a mismatching type gives E1012. A capable model without the skill tends to trust the user's description and write the ticket.
assertions: Searches Jira (project DHIS2) with short, distinct queries such as "E1074" or "enrollment geometry" and considers closed issues, or states explicitly that it could not search and gives the queries/links to run
Records the core version together with the revision (and build date if shown) from /api/system/info, not just '2.42'
Posts an enrollment with Point geometry to /api/tracker (import or importMode=VALIDATE) on a program whose featureType is POINT and reports that it is accepted (no E1074)

Runs at least one isolating variant that changes exactly one thing, and states that E1074 appears when the referenced program has no feature type set (e.g. the Malaria case diagnosis program qDkgAbB5Jlk), as opposed to POINT (accepted) or NONE (E1012)
Concludes that the bug does not reproduce as described and does NOT produce a ticket asserting that programs with Feature type = Point reject enrollment geometry
Tells the user to check the featureType of the exact program UID in their payload through the API (e.g. GET /api/programs/<uid>?fields=featureType), or to send the payload, before anything is filed
Deletes any tracked entities/enrollments it created, or states that it only ran validation dry runs or used a disposable instance that is discarded

evals.prompt: Pretty sure Data Visualizer is broken on 2.42. I made a pivot table with ANC 1st visit and ANC 2nd visit on columns, the four districts Bo, Bombali, Bonthe and Kailahun on rows, and Last 12 months as the filter. In Options I ticked 'Show column sub-totals' and 'Show row sub-totals' as well as the totals. The totals appear but there isn't a single subtotal anywhere. Same thing on the Sierra Leone demo. Please file a Jira bug for the DV team.
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as expected behaviour, not a bug: subtotals only render when an axis carries two or more dimensions; here each axis has one dimension (dx on columns, ou on rows), so a subtotal would equal the total and none is drawn. Does not write a ticket. Explains how to get subtotals (e.g. move period from filter onto rows alongside org unit, or add a second dimension on columns), and if it verifies on an instance it builds the config through the API with fixed periods, shows the one-dimension vs two-dimension contrast, and deletes the ZZTEST object. Reply is short.
evals.notes: Not-a-bug case: the skill's documented subtotal-layout trap; correct outcome is no ticket.
assertions: Concludes that this is expected behaviour (or a layout/configuration issue), not a defect, and does NOT produce a Jira ticket or ticket file for it
States that subtotals only render when an axis carries two or more dimensions, and that this layout has a single dimension on each axis (data on columns, org units on rows, period only as a filter)
Gives a concrete layout change that makes subtotals appear, e.g. moving Period from the filter onto rows together with Organisation unit (or adding a second dimension to columns)
Does not claim the behaviour is a regression, a known Jira bug, or a Data Visualizer defect in 2.42

If it verifies on an instance, it creates the test visualization through the API with a ZZTEST-style name and fixed periods (e.g. 202601) rather than LAST_12_MONTHS, and deletes it afterwards; if it does not verify, it does not claim to have reproduced anything
Keeps the reply short (no ticket-style Versions/Steps/Actual/Expected sections)

evals.prompt: Our reporting pipeline creates pivot tables with POST /api/visualizations (just the data items, periods, org units and the columns/rows/filters layout). They open fine in Data Visualizer on 2.43, but when users click Download and pick any format nothing happens, and the browser console shows TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 't.toUpperCase'). Tables saved from the DV UI download fine. Is this core or the app? Which DV version is on the instance and is it the latest on the App Hub? Has anyone reported it? If it's real, write the ticket. You can use a disposable Sierra Leone 2.43 instance at {{DHIS2_BASE_URL}} (user {{DHIS2_USERNAME}}, password {{DHIS2_PASSWORD}}).
evals.expected_output: Checks Jira first with the DV component ("[App] Data visualizer") and short symptom terms (toUpperCase, download), including closed issues. Records core version/revision from /api/system/info, the installed DV version from /dhis-web-data-visualizer/manifest.webapp fetched with an authenticated session (302 to login otherwise), and the newest App Hub version via /api/appHub/v2/apps?query=Data%20Visualizer, noting channel and minDhisVersion. Creates a ZZTEST visualization through the API with only dimensions/layout, reads it back with fields=:owner, reproduces the crash (console capture); isolating variant: the same object with only aggregationType: DEFAULT added downloads fine (the server fills displayDensity/fontSize/hideEmptyRowItems/digitGroupSeparator defaults itself; numberType is irrelevant; verified 2.42.6 and 2.43.1). Attributes to the DV app, not core (API accepts and serves the object). Ticket in template; expected result: DV defaults missing display options instead of throwing. Deletes ZZTEST objects and confirms none remain.
evals.notes: App-side bug: version triage (manifest behind auth, App Hub query form and channel), API-built saved object with :owner read-back, and one-field-set isolating variant. Still present in source in November 2026: data-visualizer-app v101.6.5 useDownload.js passes visualization.aggregationType to @dhis2/analytics withAggregationType(), which calls value.toUpperCase().
assertions: Reads the installed DV version from /dhis-web-data-visualizer/manifest.webapp using an authenticated session or basic auth (or notes the manifest redirects to login when unauthenticated)

Queries the App Hub through the instance proxy with /api/appHub/v2/apps?query=<name> (not /apps/<id>) and reports the newest version together with its channel, stating whether the installed version is the latest stable
Searches Jira restricted to the Data Visualizer component ("[App] Data visualizer") with short symptom terms such as toUpperCase or download, and reports status/fixVersions of any candidate
Creates the test visualization through the API with a ZZTEST-style name and reads it back with fields=:owner to confirm the dimensions, items, periods and org units survived
Isolates the trigger to the missing aggregationType: the same object with only aggregationType set (e.g. DEFAULT) downloads, while adding other display fields such as numberType does not fix it
Attributes the defect to the Data Visualizer app, not core, because the API accepts and returns the object and the failure is a client-side exception
Expected Result says DV should default a missing aggregationType (or otherwise download successfully) instead of throwing, rather than asking the API to reject such objects
Deletes all ZZTEST visualizations in the same turn and re-runs the name:like:ZZTEST listing to confirm it returns nothing

evals.prompt: A colleague drafted this bug report (attached, evals/files/draft-ticket-systemsettings.md) and wants it in Jira today. Can you turn it into a proper ticket? I don't have time to re-test anything right now, just make it something the core team can act on.
evals.expected_output: Rewrites the draft into the ticket template: one-line title naming the broken thing and trigger (GET /api/systemSettings/<nonexistent key> returns HTTP 500 with an HTML stack trace instead of 404); Versions table with 2.42.5.2 and a gap marked for revision/build; a duplicate-search line that does not pretend a search was run (either runs one if Jira is available, or states it has not been done); numbered imperative steps using any nonexistent key; Actual Result with the observed 500 + NotFoundException line and the POST 404 E1005 contrast as the isolating comparison, no sub-headings; Expected Result: 404 JSON with E1005 on GET, matching POST. Drops the process narrative, the priority guess, the unverified 'all settings endpoints / userSettings' generalisation and the speculative Spring/jakarta causes (at most a 2–3 sentence labelled hypothesis). Notes the key does not exist, so not-found is correct and only the status code/body is wrong. Flags what should be re-verified on a public play instance before filing.
evals.notes: Writing-only case: template and length discipline, separating findings from speculation, and not fabricating a duplicate search or reproduction that was not done.
assertions: Produces a markdown ticket whose section headings appear in this order: Versions, Steps to Reproduce, Actual Result, Expected Result (programmatically checkable), with no sub-headings inside Actual Result

Every numbered step is one imperative instruction of fewer than 20 words with no explanation or rationale (programmatically checkable for length); a step that runs a request and names what to check in its output (e.g. 'Run `curl …` and note the status') counts as one step

Frames the defect as the wrong response for a nonexistent key (HTTP 500 + HTML stack trace on GET vs 404 JSON E1005 on POST) and does not claim the CORS setting itself is missing or that keyCorsWhitelist should exist
Expected Result states the concrete response — HTTP 404 with a JSON body carrying E1005 for the GET, consistent with the POST — not a vague 'should not give a 500 / should work properly'
Removes the priority/severity guess and the investigation narrative (the hour spent changing headers, the order endpoints were tried)

Does not present the unverified generalisation ('all systemSettings endpoints', 'userSettings too') or the Spring/jakarta/Tomcat speculation as findings; any cause hypothesis is at most two or three sentences and explicitly labelled as a hypothesis

Does not fabricate a Jira duplicate search or a play-instance reproduction: either actually runs the search, or states in the ticket/reply that the duplicate search and a re-test on a public instance are still to be done

Replaces the private hostname in the steps with a public demo instance or a generic '<base>' placeholder, and uses either the public demo credentials (admin/district) or <user>/<password> placeholders (never credentials from the reporter's instance); the whole ticket is under roughly 350 words excluding the Versions table
